charts.title: How the flaw was found: a control that should have collapsed did not.
charts.takeaway: Round two found a threshold at a benefit-to-cost ratio of 9, but shuffled producers survived at 0.37. With the producer's own share removed, local producers topped out at 0.48, under the 0.5 bar.
charts.n: Round two: 100 by 100 grid, 1,200 generations, 6 runs per point. Round three: 100 by 100 grid, 1,000 generations, 5 runs per point. Shuffled control: 20 runs in each round.

steps.label: Grid of producers and cheaters
steps.detail: Producers pay a cost c to make a good worth b, shared over a 3 by 3 box of cells. Cheaters pay nothing.

steps.label: Round two: threshold at ratio 9
steps.detail: Local producers first reached a share of 0.5 at b/c of 9, at every b tried.

steps.label: Shuffled control: 0.37
steps.detail: Positions shuffled every generation, so neighbours are strangers. It should fall to 0. Mean of 20 runs at a ratio of 20.

steps.label: Cause: a ninth of its own good
steps.detail: The box counted the producer itself, so producing paid back b/9. That beats the cost once b/c passes 9, with no neighbours needed.

steps.label: Round three: goods to others only
steps.detail: The producer is taken out of its own box. Both versions run side by side up to a ratio of 400.

steps.label: Rule: local share reaches 0.5 at some ratio
Cooperation persists with goods to others only
steps.detail: Highest local share 0.48, at a ratio of 400.

charts.title: Round two, own goods included: producer share against the benefit-to-cost ratio.
charts.takeaway: Every curve is at 0 up to a ratio of 8 and crosses 0.5 at 9 (0.52, 0.66 and 0.88 for b of 1, 2 and 4). 9 is the number of cells in the goods box.
charts.units: final producer share: share of grid cells holding a producer at the end of a run, averaged over runs; 0 means cheaters took the grid
charts.n: 100 by 100 grid, 1,200 generations, 6 runs per point; 9 ratios at each of 3 values of the benefit b
charts.no_interval: The result file holds the mean over runs at each point, with no spread.
charts.baseline: Shuffled control at a ratio of 20, drawn in the next chart
charts.threshold: Persistence: mean final share of 0.5 or more. Forecast threshold between 7 and 12.

y.label: final producer share (1 means producers took the grid)

charts.title: Round two at a ratio of 20: local producers against the shuffled control.
charts.takeaway: Local producers end at 1.00. Shuffled producers, which should end at 0, end at 0.37 on average (0.26 to 0.52). Space is not what keeps them alive.
charts.units: final producer share: share of grid cells holding a producer at the end of a run, averaged over runs; 0 means cheaters took the grid

charts.interval: 5th to 95th percentile of the shuffled-control runs
charts.baseline: Shuffled arm: every position shuffled before each generation, then the local rules applied
charts.threshold: Local share above the control's 95th percentile (0.52). It held, yet the control was expected near 0.

axis.label: final producer share (0 means cheaters took the grid)

charts.title: Round three at b of 2: the same model with and without the producer's own share.
charts.takeaway: With own goods included, local producers reach 0.70 at a ratio of 9 and shuffled producers reach 1.0 by 30. With goods to others only, local producers reach 0.48 at 400 and never cross 0.5.

charts.threshold: Persistence: mean final share of 0.5 or more at some ratio, with goods to others only
charts.ruled_out: Persistence of local producers up to a ratio of 400 when goods go to others only: the highest share is 0.483, below 0.5

charts.takeaway: 10 of 13 rules held and 1 could not be tested. Round two's threshold rules held for the wrong reason; round three's rule that cooperation persists somewhere failed.
